request.spec:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Grace days are in, and changing the sheet's today now closes overdue periods automatically. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**The setting.** `grace-days` is a new setting. It takes a whole number of days, blank turns it off, and it has no from-date. It shows in the settings form with an "off" placeholder and its own error message, and saving it writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=grace-days value=<days>`.

**Auto-close.** A new step, `period/AutoClosePeriods.java`, runs in the today change (`today.PUT.yml`) right after the new today is saved and before the rollup lines. When grace days are on, it closes each open period whose to-date plus the grace days falls before the new today, earliest to-date first. Each one is fixed exactly as a close by hand would be, using the same code, and writes `PERIOD_CLOSED … auto=yes`.

**One decision to check.** If the person changing today isn't allowed to close periods on the sheet, the today change still goes through but those periods stay open. The request and the tests don't cover this case. The other option is to refuse the whole today change instead.

Two smaller points:
- Closing a period by hand writes the same line as before, without `auto=`.
- To share the close logic, I moved it out of `ClosePeriod` and `RecordPeriodClosed` into small helpers that the manual close and the auto-close both call. The manual close works as it did.
